messages.subject: Make engine for knitr
parts: Has anyone created a make engine for knitr. If not I will give it a try.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Make engine for knitr
parts:
Do you mean putting a Makefile in a code chunk? I feel people might be
more comfortable to use Make with a separate Makefile. You can run
shell scripts in knitr if the Makefile is ready, though. For example,

```{r engine='sh'}
make
make install
```

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Make engine for knitr
parts: Here is an usage scenario. I use software pipelines that uses make. If knitr can interpret my make code in the code chunk, the whole pipeline can be a single Rmd file that run make on demand. This will also have the advantage of dependency checking of the make that currently not possible using shell engine of knitr. This will be highly useful in real documented makefile maintenance. I modified the engine.R file to use make code, but don't understand enough knitr to create the syntax highlighting.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Make engine for knitr
parts: Thank you Yihui. That would be wonderful. .Rmd syntax highlighting is what needed most. Also, two other things will be fantastic for big data analysis pipelines. The user should be able to set the engine options. For e.g.  to run the code in SMP parallel mode, the use can set "-j" option. I also see to there is a way to give the full path name of the engine software. In HPC scenario, for e.g. in sun grid engine controlled cluster, there is  command 'qmake' that takes a gnu makefile and distribute the job automatically over a cluster. So if a chunk can redefine "make" command as "qmake" when needed, the .Rmd file can now carry out distributed data processing over cluster. That will be fantastic.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Make engine for knitr
parts:
I thought for a while on this issue, and I think it may not worth
inventing a separate engine for make. I just tweaked the existing
engine `cat`, which allows you to write the code chunk to a file, e.g.
a Makefile. Then you are free to run shell scripts (make, or make -j,
or qmake, or whatever). Syntax highlighting is fairly easy with Pandoc
and the rmarkdown package (http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com). The only
thing to remember is that the default highlight theme does not seem to
work for Makefile, but other themes seem to work very well. Here is an
R Markdown document, which you can compile in RStudio if you want (you
need the development version of knitr:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr):

---
title: "Document Title"
author: "Yihui Xie"
date: '`r Sys.Date()`'
output:
html_document:
highlight: tango
---

Test.

```{r engine='cat', engine.opts=list(lang='makefile', file='Makefile')}
# a comment
foo:
echo "abc"

bar:
rm xyz.log && pdflatex xyz.tex
```

Run make.

```{r engine='sh'}
make foo
```

For some reason, Gmail does not allow me to write tabs here. I think
you are familiar with Makefiles, so you should know that there must be
tabs in the first code chunk.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
